advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a producer-liveness anchor to test_real_repository_dockerfiles_match_the_pyproject_pin (assert at least one 'astral-sh/uv' line was matched before trusting the per-line assertions).
evidence: tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py:345 `for path in sorted(REPO_ROOT.glob("infra/compose/Dockerfile.*")):`
tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py:347-348 `if "astral-sh/uv" not in line:` / `continue`
tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py:349 `assert f"astral-sh/uv:{version}" in line`
ABSENCE: no counter/flag asserting at least one uv reference line was inspected; if glob or the substring filter yields nothing the assertion never runs and the test is green.
advisory.finding: test_real_repository_dockerfiles_match_the_pyproject_pin is a fail-open oracle: it only asserts on lines containing 'astral-sh/uv' and never asserts that any such line was actually found, so it passes vacuously if the glob matches no Dockerfile or the uv COPY line is renamed/removed — the exact skew it is meant to detect.
scenarios: A future refactor moves the uv COPY out of infra/compose/Dockerfile.* or changes the image path substring; the test keeps passing while the pin is unverified.
advisory.suggested_fix: Collect matched uv lines into a list and `assert matched, "no uv references found"` before/after the per-line tag assertions.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make test_real_repository_dockerfiles_do_not_float_the_uv_tag drive check_dockerfiles(REPO_ROOT) (or assert _dockerfiles(REPO_ROOT) is non-empty) so it cannot pass when nothing was scanned.
evidence: tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py:332-337 list comprehension over `_gate_module()._dockerfiles(REPO_ROOT)` with `if ":latest" in line and line.lstrip().startswith(("FROM", "COPY --from="))`
tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py:338 `assert not offenders, f"floating :latest toolchain tags: {offenders}"`

ABSENCE: the test reimplements floating-tag detection rather than invoking check_dockerfiles/check_repo, and never asserts _dockerfiles(REPO_ROOT) returned a non-empty set, so a broken discovery producer yields an empty offenders list and a green pass.
advisory.finding: test_real_repository_dockerfiles_do_not_float_the_uv_tag re-derives the ':latest' detection in-process (convergence twin) instead of driving the gate, and its `assert not offenders` passes vacuously if `_dockerfiles(REPO_ROOT)` returns an empty list — no liveness check that any Dockerfile was scanned.
scenarios: _dockerfiles's skip-set or glob changes and returns nothing; the test passes while the real tree is never scanned for floating tags.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert `_gate_module()._dockerfiles(REPO_ROOT)` is non-empty, or invoke `check_dockerfiles(REPO_ROOT)` and assert it returns no findings, rather than re-deriving the detection logic.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider pinning the uv images by digest alongside the tag (`ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.7@sha256:...`) in the three production Dockerfiles for provenance, not just version agreement.
evidence: `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.7 /uv /usr/local/bin/uv`
The gate's own docstring notes the digest+tag form `uv:0.12.7@sha256:...` is 'the strongest form and stays allowed' but the three shipped Dockerfiles use tag-only.
test_dockerfile_uv_tag_with_matching_digest_is_allowed confirms digest is optional, not required.
advisory.finding: The three production uv images are pinned by mutable tag (`ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.7`) with no accompanying digest, so the pulled bytes are not provenance-locked; a re-pushed or compromised upstream `0.12.7` tag would be consumed silently.
scenarios: Upstream ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.7 tag is force-pushed or the registry is compromised, delivering a different binary under the same tag.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/decide whether base images should also be digest-pinned, since the gate only strictly single-sources uv and leaves base-image tags mutable.
evidence: `if not is_uv:\n        return None` in `_check_dockerfile_reference` — non-uv images pass once they carry any non-latest tag.
test_dockerfile_non_uv_digest_without_a_tag_is_allowed and the docstring: 'the uv rule is deliberately narrower than "every image needs a tag"'.
advisory.finding: The gate enforces the uv version tag but does not require any digest for base images (e.g. `FROM python:3.12-slim`), leaving base-image provenance floating-by-mutable-tag repo-wide.
scenarios: A base image tag like python:3.12-slim is updated upstream, changing the transitive OS/library dependency set of the built image without any repo change.

evidence: tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py:346-349: `if "astral-sh/uv" not in line:` / `continue` / `assert f"astral-sh/uv:{version}" in line`
ABSENCE: no assertion that at least one uv reference was found across the scanned Dockerfiles (search for `assert version`/count guard returned no matches)
Litmus: the test produces its PASS verdict in the world 'no uv reference exists', which is indistinguishable from 'checked and clean'.
advisory.finding: test_real_repository_dockerfiles_match_the_pyproject_pin is a fail-open oracle: it skips every line not containing 'astral-sh/uv' and only asserts on matching lines, so if no uv reference exists in any scanned Dockerfile (rename, removal, or typo in the repository path) the assertion never executes and the test passes vacuously. It cannot distinguish 'all uv images correctly pinned to required-version' from 'the uv reference disappeared entirely'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Accumulate seen uv lines and assert the count is non-zero after the loop, e.g. `seen = [l for path in ... for l in ... if 'astral-sh/uv' in l]; assert seen, 'no uv reference found'; for l in seen: assert f'astral-sh/uv:{version}' in l`.

evidence: tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py:345-349: `for path in sorted(REPO_ROOT.glob("infra/compose/Dockerfile.*")):` / `if "astral-sh/uv" not in line: continue` / `assert f"astral-sh/uv:{version}" in line`
ABSENCE: there is no `assert matched` / non-empty-count check establishing that at least one uv reference line was inspected before the loop's per-line assertion is trusted.
advisory.finding: test_real_repository_dockerfiles_match_the_pyproject_pin passes vacuously (fail-open oracle): its only assertion is nested inside `for path in glob(...)` / `for line in ...` guarded by `if "astral-sh/uv" not in line: continue`, with no check that any uv reference was actually found. If the glob matches no Dockerfile, or no line contains `astral-sh/uv` (e.g. a file rename, repository move, or comment-only reference), the loop body never asserts and the test reports success — it cannot distinguish 'all images correctly pinned' from 'no image inspected'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Collect matched uv lines into a list and assert it is non-empty (e.g. `matched = [line for path in ... for line in ... if "astral-sh/uv" in line]; assert matched; for line in matched: assert f"astral-sh/uv:{version}" in line`).

evidence: tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py:332-338: builds `offenders` list-comprehension and asserts `not offenders`
ABSENCE: no lower-bound assertion that `_dockerfiles(REPO_ROOT)` returned a non-empty list or that a uv line was among them
tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py:332-337: `offenders = [ ... for path in _gate_module()._dockerfiles(REPO_ROOT) ... if ":latest" in line and line.lstrip().startswith(("FROM", "COPY --from="))]`
The production path under review is `check_dockerfiles` / `_check_dockerfile_reference` (scripts/check_uv_pin.py:455-510), which this test does not call — only `_dockerfiles` is reused.
advisory.finding: test_real_repository_dockerfiles_do_not_float_the_uv_tag asserts an empty offenders list, which is also empty when zero Dockerfiles are discovered or no FROM/COPY lines exist; combined with the sibling test's vacuity, neither real-repo test asserts the scan actually inspected a uv reference.
